h: From indoor walls to real gritstone
p: Sheffield has a proper climbing pedigree. The gritstone edges of the Peak District, like Stanage Edge, are just west of the city, and generations of climbers have learned their trade on them. A first session at Rock Up is a fun way to see whether your young adventurer has caught the bug, and who knows, it could be the start of something. Tips for the day: wear stretchy clothes, keep nails short and tie long hair back.

Getting to Meadowhall is easy: the Meadowhall Interchange brings together trains, buses and the Supertram, so you can leave the car at home if you prefer. Once you're done, Magna Science Adventure Centre is just down the road at Templeborough in Rotherham, inside a giant former steelworks, with hands-on exhibits about earth, air, fire and water. It's a brilliant follow-up for kids who still have energy to burn.

Back in the city, Kelham Island Museum tells Sheffield's steel story with the mighty River Don Engine, a huge steam engine that still gets fired up from time to time. The Winter Garden in the city centre is a huge glasshouse full of plants from around the world, and the Millennium Gallery next door is free. Sheffield Botanical Gardens, with its restored Victorian glass pavilions, is a peaceful spot for a picnic. Whichever way you go, it's a great city for a family day out.
